item.title: Elusive builders of nearly perfect hexagonal tunnel fossils were probably small crustaceans—not worms
item.description: [Open Source Software] Keyword: FOSS — For more than 170 years, paleontologists have been trying to solve the mystery of what created the strangely uniform hexagonal tunnels found in fossils. In a new study published in Earth Science Reviews, a team of researchers pored over the evidence and concluded that the most likely culprit was a type of arthropod—probably a small crustacean. This challenges a long-standing idea that a worm-like creature may have created the tunnels.
